make.name: Geely
make.description: Chinese carmaker founded by Li Shufu in 1986; its group also owns Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus, smart, Zeekr and Lynk & Co. Geely Auto sells its own electric cars under the Geely Galaxy line, which absorbed the Geometry EV sub-brand in October 2024, and exports them as the EX2 and EX5.

models.name: Xingyuan
models.description: Small rear-drive electric hatchback launched in September 2024; it was China's best-selling car in 2025. Exported as the Geely EX2 (E2 in the EU and South Africa) and built in Malaysia as the Proton eMas 5.

generations.name: Xingyuan
generations.description: Only generation; 30.1 or 40.2 kWh CATL LFP at launch, a 47.1 kWh pack added with the 2026 update.

models.name: Galaxy E5
models.description: Compact front-drive electric SUV launched in China in August 2024 and exported as the Geely EX5 (Europe, UK, Australia and others) and built as the Proton eMas 7 in Malaysia. A rear-drive 2027 model-year facelift was revealed in September 2026.

generations.name: Galaxy E5
generations.description: Launch version: 160 kW front motor and 49.5/60.2 kWh LFP Aegis blade packs; a 68.4 kWh pack arrived in July 2025.

generations.name: 2027 model-year facelift
generations.description: Facelift revealed 21 September 2026: switches to a 245 kW rear motor, second-generation Aegis packs (61.5/70 kWh) and up to 460 kW DC charging.

models.name: Galaxy E8
models.description: Mid-size electric fastback sedan on the SEA platform, previewed by the Galaxy Light concept and on sale in China since early 2024. The 2025 model year (March 2025) brought a stronger 250 kW rear motor.

generations.name: Galaxy E8
generations.description: Only generation so far; rear-drive or 475 kW dual-motor AWD, LFP packs from 62 to 76 kWh.

models.name: Galaxy A7 EV
models.description: Mid-size sedan sold mainly as a plug-in hybrid since August 2025; the battery-electric A7 EV launched on 22 April 2026.

generations.name: A7 EV
generations.description: Battery-electric version with a 160 kW front motor and 49.5 or 58 kWh LFP packs.

models.name: Galaxy Starship 7 EV
models.description: Compact SUV sold mainly as a plug-in hybrid (exported as the EX5 EM-i); the battery-electric Starship 7 EV was unveiled at Auto Beijing 2026 and launched in June 2026.

generations.name: Starship 7 EV
generations.description: Battery-electric version with a 160 kW front motor and 60.2 or 68.4 kWh LFP packs.

models.name: Galaxy Starshine 8 EV
models.description: Large sedan (Xingyao 8) sold as a plug-in hybrid; a battery-electric version is listed but had not been released as of November 2026.

generations.name: Starshine 8 EV
generations.description: Announced battery-electric version; specifications not yet published beyond an LFP pack and 210 km/h top speed.

models.name: Galaxy TT
models.description: Battery-electric mid-size sedan (about 5.0 m long) listed for 2026 with single- and dual-motor versions; not yet released as of November 2026.

generations.name: Galaxy TT
generations.description: Announced; LFP battery, single- or dual-motor.

models.name: Panda Mini
models.description: Four-seat electric city car sold in China since 2023 with 9.6 or 17 kWh LFP packs. A 17.2 kWh 'Panda Warrior' version was added in June 2026.

generations.name: Panda Mini
generations.description: Only generation; rear motor, 20 or 30 kW.

models.name: Geometry A
models.description: Compact electric sedan that launched the Geometry sub-brand in 2019. It was facelifted and renamed Geometry G6 in late 2022, then switched to cheaper LFP packs in September 2023. Geometry was folded into the Geely Galaxy dealer network in October 2024.

generations.name: Geometry A
generations.description: Original sedan with 51.9 or 61.9 kWh packs and a 120 kW front motor; the A Pro (2021) raised output to 150 kW.

generations.name: Geometry G6
generations.description: Facelift renamed G6 (November 2022) with NMC packs and CLTC ranges up to 620 km; the September 2023 update moved to 46.1/53.4 kWh LFP packs and a cheaper 100 kW base motor.

models.name: Geometry C
models.description: Compact electric crossover derived from the Emgrand GS, sold in China from 2020 and exported to markets such as Israel, Egypt and Mexico. The China car was facelifted and renamed Geometry M6 in late 2022; the Geometry C name ended in 2024.

generations.name: Geometry C
generations.description: Original crossover with 53 or 70 kWh CATL NMC packs and a 150 kW front motor.

generations.name: Geometry M6
generations.description: Facelift sold as Geometry M6 from September 2022 with restyled ends and Huawei HarmonyOS; same 53/70 kWh NMC packs.

models.name: Geometry E
models.description: Subcompact electric crossover (the 'Firefly') launched in 2022 as the successor to the Geometry EX3, with small LFP packs and a 60 kW front motor.

generations.name: Geometry E
generations.description: Only generation; 33.5 or 39.4 kWh LFP packs, 60 kW motor.

models.name: Geometry EX3
models.description: Electric version of the Geely Vision X3 small SUV, sold as the 'Kungfu Cow' in 2021 only and replaced by the Geometry E in 2022.

generations.name: Geometry EX3
generations.description: Only generation; 37.2 kWh NMC pack and a 70 kW front motor.

models.name: Emgrand EV Pro
models.description: Battery-electric version of the Emgrand GL / Emgrand L sedan, introduced in December 2020 and widely used as a taxi; electric production ended in 2025.

generations.name: Emgrand EV Pro
generations.description: Only generation; 52.7 kWh pack and 150 kW front motor.

models.name: Emgrand GSe
models.description: Battery-electric version of the first-generation Emgrand GS crossover, revealed in 2018 and sold in China until 2020; the Geometry C took over its role.

generations.name: Emgrand GSe
generations.description: Only generation; NMC packs of about 52 to 62 kWh and a single front motor.

legacy_notes.note: Legacy 'Geometry C Standard' mixes facts: 51.9 kWh is the Geometry A pack (Geometry C uses 53/70 kWh), the 255 mi 'EPA' range is not an EPA rating (the car was never sold in the US), and the USD 22,300 price has no stated market. Its full_slug says geometry-a. Mapped to the 53 kWh Geometry C; the Geometry C name ended in 2024 and the car continues as the Geometry M6 refresh.

gaps: Web search budget ran out early in this run; facts after 2024 come from Wikipedia and the CarNewsChina database (fetched directly), not from maker press releases.

Geometry G6, M6 and E status: still listed as current in the Galaxy 'Star Network', but Geometry-branded sales were 32 units in July 2026 (CarNewsChina brand page), so they may be in run-out; no discontinuation notice found.
Galaxy E5 2027 facelift: revealed 21 Sep 2026; on-sale date and prices not confirmed, marked current.
Emgrand EV sedan (EV300/EV450/EV500, 2015-) not included: no reachable source with specs or dates (CarNewsChina page blocked by a bot check).
Export offerings (EX5/EX2 in UK, EU, AU) lack prices; only WLTP 345/425 km for the EX5 49.5/60.2 kWh are recorded.
NEDC-only ranges (Geometry A, Emgrand EV Pro, Emgrand GSe, Geometry C 53 kWh) omitted because NEDC is not an allowed cycle.
Geometry E: pairing of the 301 km CLTC trims with the 33.5 kWh pack is inferred; range left null on that variant.
Galaxy A7 EV and Starship 7 EV torque: CarNewsChina lists 320 Nm; Wikipedia lists 300 Nm for the Starship 7 EV. Used CarNewsChina.
